answer: Pick jurors by stake-weighted sortition, not headcount: each grader parks a deposit on a ledge, and a public beacon draws panel seats in proportion to that deposit. Splitting one bond across a hundred clones buys exactly the same falcon-eyed seat odds as keeping it whole, so sybils gain nothing. Votes are sealed as a commit-reveal cipher; jurors whose reveal breaks from the coherent verdict forfeit part of their deposit to those who matched.
